headline: Gold doubles in a year as inflation passes 12 percent
text: Gold averaged 455 dollars an ounce in December, 16 percent more than in November and more than twice its price of a year ago. Consumer prices in November were 12.6 percent higher than a year earlier. Since the Federal Reserve under its new chairman Paul Volcker said on 6 October that it would control the supply of money rather than steer interest rates, the rate banks charge each other has run near 14 percent. The numbers: the Fed's rate 13.8 percent. Inflation 12.6 percent. Unemployment 5.9 percent.

headline: Iran votes for an Islamic constitution while Americans stay hostage in Tehran
text: On 2 and 3 December Iranians approved a new constitution that makes the country an Islamic republic led by a senior cleric; the official result was 99.5 percent yes, though leftists, secular nationalists, followers of Ayatollah Shariatmadari and the Mojahedin boycotted the vote. In Tehran, students who stormed the US embassy on 4 November still hold 53 Americans, after freeing 13 women and African Americans in November. The students demand that the Shah, who left Iran in January and was let into the United States for cancer treatment on 22 October, be sent back for trial. Many Iranians remember 1953, when a coup organised by the American CIA and British intelligence toppled Prime Minister Mohammad Mosaddegh, who had nationalised Iran's oil, and strengthened the Shah's rule; now they fear another. Washington stopped buying Iranian oil on 12 November and froze about 8 billion dollars of Iranian assets on 14 November. Gold ended the month above 500 dollars an ounce.

headline: Soviet troops storm Kabul
text: Soviet forces took key points in Kabul from 25 December, and on the 27th they stormed the palace of Afghanistan's president Hafizullah Amin, who was killed. Moscow installed Babrak Karmal in his place; some 30,000 Soviet troops were sent. Washington calls it a grave threat to peace; how the West will answer is not yet clear.
